local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 New Mexico's counties elect, on the partisan ballot, a probate judge in each of the 33 counties, the county commissioners whose terms are up (county councilors in Los Alamos County), a sheriff in 31 counties, an assessor in 32, a county clerk in Eddy and Lincoln counties and a treasurer in Lincoln County; magistrate judges are elected in 32 counties and a municipal judge in Los Alamos County, thirteen district judgeships and two judgeships of the Bernalillo County Metropolitan Court are filled for unexpired terms, and sitting district and metropolitan court judges face yes-or-no retention votes (40 of them). Cities, towns and villages, school boards and other local districts elect at the Regular Local Election in November of odd-numbered years, and a municipality that has not joined it at the Municipal Officer Election in March of even-numbered years, so none of their offices is on this ballot.

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List: 166 contests for county offices in all 33 counties (commissioners and councilors, sheriffs, assessors, clerks, a treasurer and probate judges) and 122 for local judges, shown with the judges (magistrate judges: 66; district court judges: 13; metropolitan court judges: 2; a municipal judge: 1; retention votes: 40), 367 names in all, 6 of them declared write-in candidates. The list was read whole and again county by county and the two readings agree; 5 names it marks Withdrawn or Disqualified are left off. The proclamation lists one office nobody is on the list for (County Commissioner, District 2, Curry County), kept here with no candidate. Not loaded: ballot questions (constitutional amendments, bond questions and any county question), which a candidate list does not carry; the June 2 primaries for these offices; and any office put on the ballot after the proclamation for which nobody is listed.

gaps.w: offices added after the proclamation that nobody filed for
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's candidate list shows a contest only when someone is listed for it, so the checklist of offices is the proclamation of January 26, 2026; an office put on the ballot after that date for which no candidate is listed would not be seen here.

gaps.w: elections that conservancy districts and other bodies run themselves
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's November list carries no contest for any city, school district or special district, and the Local Election Act leaves conservancy districts out of the Regular Local Election; an election such a body holds on its own is not on the list and would have to be read from that body's own notice.
